Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our offer for a price of €6.05 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. 

To give you some background on our current situation and market conditions, AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost. Lastly, PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost. 

Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days. We look forward to continuing our partnership with your team and supplying your needs from our extensive inventory.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

move.subject: Volume-tier offer for stainless bar
move.body:
Dear Mr Aigner,

Thank you for your offer and the explanation of the alloy, labour and processing cost movements. I appreciate your willingness to continue supplying us from your inventory. For this business, please quote a dedicated volume tier rather than the price for a shorter arrangement.

The annual quantity is 94800 kg, with that annual quantity applying in each year of the proposed 24-month term. I have attached our latest shared monthly forecast; see the figures below for the supporting demand information.

Our proposal is EUR 4.58 per kg, fixed without a price adjustment clause, with payment at 90 days net and a contract term of 24 months. Delivery remains DAP.

Please review this package against the annual volume and the longer term, and confirm the volume-tier price you can offer on that basis.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

Dear customer,
Thank you very much for your message - it is always a pleasure to hear from you, and we are glad to help wherever we can.
We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows.
Our terms: a price of €5.57 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 24 months, a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404.
Here is the background.
We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account.
Thank you for sharing the updated forecast; we are pleased to support your volume with a 24-month agreement.
Please note that for a 24-month term, we must include an AS-14404 index clause to manage raw material volatility, as a fixed price is not feasible over this period.
We can extend the payment terms to 60 days and offer a revised price of €5.57 per kg based on this structure.
Alternatively, with Zahlungsziel 60 days net: €5.54 per unit.
Our price follows our main cost drivers: AS-14404, PPI-C2431, LCI-C.
A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the price.
Which volume can you commit to?
We can offer a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404, AS-14404, AS-14404.
Our standard Zahlungsziel is 30 days net.
And while we are at it: our whole range is at your disposal, so if there is anything else on your list, just send it over - we are happy to quote.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

move.subject: Re: Bar stock agreement – revised price proposal
move.body:
Dear Mr Aigner,

Thank you for reducing your price and retaining payment at 90 days net. I understand your point that the material cover does not span the full agreement and that you therefore require an AS-14404 clause in your offer. I am not treating that clause as agreed.

To answer your volume question, the binding quantity we can offer is 94800 kg per year, applying in each year of the proposed 24-month agreement. Please base the volume tier on that quantity; the forecast already shared provides the monthly profile.

You confirmed the purchase-order history but explained that it did not change your calculation. For this review, please also consider the published figures below for PPI-C2431, which you identify as a cost driver.

We can raise our proposal to EUR 4.93 per kg, fixed without a price adjustment clause, for 24 months with payment at 90 days net. Delivery remains DAP.

Please review this revised price against the annual commitment and the processing-cost evidence, and let me know how far you can accommodate the fixed-price package.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

We look forward to doing good business together, and our team is always there for you.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

strategy:
Supplier: Edelstahl-Service Donautal (stainless bar stockholder, group company, inside sales desk). Its letter of
2026-07-06 says its nickel/alloy requirement is covered at fixed prices until March 2027. It always asks "Which volume
can you commit to?" and for the volume forecast; it will insert an AS-14404 index clause itself for a 24-month term
(let it - do not propose a clause yourself); it accepts 90-day payment when we hold it.
OBSERVED MECHANIC (4 sessions): its first reply is a package answer (about the same whatever our price). After that
it mirrors OUR price move: when we move up by 0.11-0.16 EUR it moves down by about 0.85 of that; when we move by 0.01-0.02
it moves 0.03-0.05 and declares a final offer. It also goes final when we change nothing. So: anchor deep in round 1,
then move UP by about 0.14 EUR every round on the SAME package (no clause, 90 days, 24 months) with one new
verified claim each round, never touching payment or term, until the code closes. Our asks should stay below its
price each round; if the gap gets below 0.12, move to about 0.02 under its price.
Plan: ROUND 1 - state the binding fixed annual volume (case volume per year and the total over 24 months), attach
the forecast (attachments: ["forecast"]) and cite fc-latest; ask for the dedicated volume tier price. ONE sheet:
no index clause, 90 days, 24 months, level L12 (deepest, about 4.55). ROUND 2 - thank it for what it accepted, cite the
purchase-order claim, move up ~0.14 (pick the level closest to last price + 0.14, same package: if it inserted an
index clause, keep OUR package without clause - the supplier may keep offering the clause; that is fine).
ROUND 3 - cite PPI-C2431 fall (first window), move up ~0.14. ROUND 4 - cite the second PPI-C2431 window, move up
~0.11. ROUND 5 - no new claim (do not re-cite PPI-C2431: one claim per index series), move up ~0.14, ask for its best price. Code accepts when it agrees or goes final.
Tone: warm, firm, concrete, short; one argument per sentence; mention its material cover until March 2027 once
(round 2) as the reason a fixed base price over the term is reasonable. Do NOT use any AS-14404 index claim and
do not use the scorecard claim.
